monthly_review.summary: You've shifted toward faster, more intense running this month — pace improved significantly and aerobic TE increased, but volume dropped sharply compared to last month. HR rose notably, suggesting reduced recovery margin.
monthly_review.highlight: Your average pace improved by 19 sec/km despite a 8 bpm increase in average heart rate — indicating higher intensity but potentially compromised efficiency and recovery.

goal_tracker.message: You need 22.3 more km across 5 additional sessions in the remaining 23 days to match last month’s volume — averaging ~4.5 km per session.

insights.title: Efficiency declined with rising intensity
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency dropped from 13.42 to 13.19 km/hr per bpm, coinciding with a +8 bpm avg HR and +4 spm cadence — suggesting you’re working harder for less physiological return per beat.

insights.title: Zone 3–4 dominance replaced Zone 1–2 base work
insights.body: This month’s HR zone distribution shows only 20% Z1 vs 36% last month, while Z3+ jumped from 22% to 45% — signaling a sharp reduction in easy aerobic development and possible fatigue accumulation.

insights.title: Cadence increased but stride length collapsed under fatigue
insights.body: Cadence rose to 150 spm (from 146), yet stride length dropped from 72.5 cm (June 1) to 69.7 cm (June 7 long run) and as low as 68.8 cm on June 4 — likely compensating for fatigue rather than improving form.

insights.title: High-intensity micro-sessions dominate recent activity
insights.body: Three runs on June 4 totaled just 2.5 km but included a 7:03/km effort at 159 bpm (Z4), contributing disproportionately to acute load without adequate Z1/Z2 recovery balance.

recommendations.action: Do your next run as a pure Zone 2 aerobic session: 6 km at HR ≤135 bpm, cadence 146–148 spm, pace ≥550 sec/km (9:10/km).
recommendations.reason: To rebuild aerobic base and restore efficiency — your last month had 43% Z2 time vs only 32% this month, and avg efficiency has declined.

recommendations.action: Replace one upcoming run with a 20-min Z1 walk or elliptical session (HR ≤120 bpm) to lower cumulative stress before the next long run.
recommendations.reason: Your June 4 triple-session day created high acute load with minimal Z1 recovery — ground contact time increased to 330 ms on the slowest run, indicating neuromuscular fatigue.

recommendations.action: On your next 10+ km run, maintain stride length ≥72.0 cm by cueing 'light footstrike' and counting cadence every 2 min to hold 148–150 spm — no pace targets.
recommendations.reason: Stride length fell below 70 cm in 3 of 5 recent runs despite cadence gains, reflecting compromised form under fatigue — not fitness limitation.

weekly_focus.description: Re-establish Z1–Z2 physiological anchors to improve efficiency, lower HR drift, and protect form during longer efforts.
suggested_sessions: 45-min mixed Z1/Z2 progression run (first 20 min Z1, last 25 min Z2)
